tier_reason: First-party wiki page (Seastar project, Feb 2015) with a raw-data table of Seastar+DPDK memcached vs stock Memcached 1.4.17 multi-process and multi-threaded at 2-20 cores. The CPU model (2x Xeon E5-2695v3, via the linked HTTPD-benchmark page), memaslap command lines and the Seastar app (apps/memcached/memcache.cc) are public, but the compiler and flags are never stated, so it cannot be A.

corrections.caveats: Benchmark is first-party (Seastar project's own GitHub wiki), not an independent third party; the page was created and last edited Feb 19 - Mar 1, 2015 (wiki history), so it is over 11 years old; compiler and build flags are not stated (only the build/release binary path); the Seastar side runs its own userspace TCP/IP stack over DPDK kernel bypass (--network-stack native --dpdk-pmd) while stock memcached uses the Linux kernel network stack, so the gain mixes kernel bypass with the reactor design and is not an isolated reactor-vs-libevent comparison; the 4x figure is against memcached's threaded mode, which the page says suffers from lock contention (mutex_trylock busy-wait), and the page itself calls the 2x multi-process comparison 'not a fair comparison'; the multi-threaded memcached configuration is not described in the setup section; the comparison is at the whole-application (memcached) level rather than a synthetic libevent-only microbenchmark, though memcached's own event loop is libevent-based.

notes: All of the claimed numbers match the 20-CPU row exactly, and both the '4X faster than the stock threaded memcache' and 'outperforms stock memcache by 2X' sentences are on the page. The hardware field matches the HTTPD-benchmark wiki's hardware section. Metadata checks out: Apache-2.0, 9,382 stars, not a fork or archived, last commit 2026-09-25.

tier_reason: First-party bar chart in the uvloop README comparing uvloop with stock asyncio's default loop on echo servers (sockets, streams and protocol APIs at 1/10/100 KiB). The benchmark code is public (MagicStack/vmbench servers/asyncioecho.py, with --uvloop/--streams/--proto) and the linked 2016 blog post (now only on the Wayback Machine) names the CPU (Xeon E5-1620 v2), but no compiler or flags are given for the Cython/libuv build, so it cannot be A.

corrections.baseline: CPython asyncio default event loop (pure-Python SelectorEventLoop, epoll-backed on Linux)
corrections.claimed_speedup: README states 'uvloop makes asyncio 2-4x faster'. Read off the README bar chart (derived from page data): protocol API at 1 KiB ~106k uvloop vs ~43k asyncio req/s (~2.5x); sockets API at 1 KiB ~52k vs ~13.5k (~3.9x); streams API at 1 KiB ~44k vs ~17.5k (~2.5x); at 100 KiB the gap narrows to ~1.8x (protocol, ~23.5k vs ~12.8k) and ~1.4x (streams, ~12k vs ~8.8k).
corrections.hardware: Intel Xeon E5-1620 v2 @ 3.70GHz, Ubuntu Linux, Python 3.5, single-threaded servers in Docker, concurrency 10, 30 s runs (from the May 3, 2016 magic.io blog post that the README chart links to; the README itself does not restate hardware)
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark. The chart was committed on 2016-05-22 and the linked magic.io blog post (May 3, 2016) no longer resolves live; it is still readable via the Wayback Machine (2017-03-01 snapshot), which gives the CPU, OS, Python 3.5 and vmbench setup but no compiler or flags. The README chart's sockets/streams/protocol series do not appear in the blog post's own charts, so it is assumed, not proven, that they came from the same run and hardware. All numbers are read off a bar-chart image, not from text. The data is from Python 3.5, and stock asyncio has changed a lot since, so today's gap is unmeasured here. At 100 KiB messages the gain is only ~1.4-1.8x, below the '2-4x' headline. Both loops ultimately use epoll on Linux (uvloop through libuv), so this is a Python-event-loop-implementation comparison rather than a win over raw epoll. The vmbench harness was last pushed in 2018.

notes: The numbers match the chart to within chart-reading precision (the blog text itself quotes ~105,000 req/s for uvloop at 1 KiB). The baseline was changed from 'epoll' to stock asyncio's event loop, since that is what the chart labels and both sides use epoll underneath; baseline_in_list was set to false. License corrected to the dual Apache-2.0/MIT stated in the README (GitHub reports only Apache-2.0); stars (11,904), last commit (2026-07-14) and active status are verified.
